newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, range-bound.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, range-bound.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Monday as Japan's banking woes continued to weigh on market sentiment, dealers said.
They said Nikkei futures tested lows after some selling of banking shares in Tokyo.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract tested its low at 17,550 but quickly rebounded to 17,650. It ended 135 points lower at 17,645 on a turnover of 13,000 lots.
Dealers said the market was locked in a range after the dollar failed to break beyond 126 yen.

"There is obviously no clear trend. I think the market will continue to stay within a range," said a dealer with a Japanese bank. He pegged firm support and resistance for June at 17,500 and 17,800, respectively.
Dealers said the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita's speech to a group of business leaders failed to reveal fresh insight.
"There is nothing new from his speech. He just repeated the BOJ's accommodative rate stance," said a dealer with a European brokerage house.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 360.1 against its opening 353.5. Turnover was a light 893 lots.
